name: Omaports
author: Mich Nduka
description: Open dev ports on localhost in the Omarchy bar: which project holds which port, what is reachable beyond this machine, and a way to close it.

barWidget.description: Every listening port on localhost, named by the project it belongs to, with open-in-browser, copy, a terminal in the project, and kill.

schema.label: Refresh interval (seconds)
schema.description: How often the socket table is read. One `ss` call and a short walk of /proc, so this is cheap enough to leave low.

schema.label: Number next to the icon
schema.description: Dev ports counts what looks like something you are running; the other two count everything, or nothing at all.

schema.label: Turn the icon urgent when a dev port is open to the network
schema.description: A dev server bound to 0.0.0.0 is reachable from every machine on the network you are on. This is the one thing here worth interrupting you over.

schema.label: Include ports owned by other users
schema.description: Databases, daemons, and anything running as root. They are named where the port is well known, but never carry a process, because only root can see whose they are.

schema.label: Include UDP sockets
schema.description: Off by default: a dev server listens on TCP, and the UDP table is mostly mDNS and discovery chatter.

schema.label: Extra dev ports
schema.description: Ports to always count as yours, beyond the ones already recognised. Commas, spaces, and ranges all work: 7788, 9100-9110.

schema.label: Ports to hide
schema.description: Dropped from every list and every count. Same format as above.

schema.label: Ports served over HTTPS
schema.description: Ports whose links should open as https rather than http. Same format as above.

schema.label: Signal the kill action sends
schema.description: The polite signal, which a dev server usually handles by shutting down cleanly. Force kill always sends KILL regardless of this.
